items.title: Thursday briefing: What we do (and don’t) know about Alice Huang and the Nvidia affair
items.summary: In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang Good morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies. Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines. UK | Ministers are considering changing the law to force the entertainment industry to better protect women and children in the wake of the revelations over David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand. Climate | The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country. US midterms | Democrat Scott Colom has become the first Black senator in Mississippi to be elected since Reconstruction, in a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states. Europe | Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s first general strike in 14 years , setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power. Technology | Police officers risk arresting innocent people , especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found. items.title: Show HN: Lynx – open-source fully-customizable AI workspace
items.summary: I was finding that managing multiple agent threads with walls of text was getting tiring and inefficient for me and that I wanted a more visual way to interact with my agents, so I built Lynx. Lynx lets you quickly build fully custom interfaces connected to your data sources (e.g. via MCP or API) and trigger agents running on your machine from them (e.g. with Claude Code or Codex). I built it as an experiment but have found myself doing 80-90% of my work from inside Lynx. I have my own Conductor-like workspace for coding, a Mail client, a workspace for my writing, and various others for dashboards and explorations. A few things are really cool about it: - Adding buttons to a UI that trigger a Claude Code agent running on my machine (e.g. to review a PR, get started on a task from Linear, or look for typos in my text) - Iterating on the interfaces is really easy, particularly because of a point tool that let's you select what you want changed and an agent will update it live - Switching between workspaces takes a fraction of a second (much faster than e.g. switching between websites) - It's all local :) Harnesses have been moving towards native support for artifacts and MCP-UI which kind of go in this direction but I think the current models add to context fragmentation rather than actually help it, so I flipped the model on its head and built an AI workspace / harness where interactive interfaces are at the core. Calling this an AI workspace for now but honestly unsure what the proper term should be. Is this a visual harness? A hub for personal software? Keen to hear feedback about the conceptual model and what others have done that might be similar! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50461775 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
